criteria.text: `fetchFeed`'s item extraction, given an `rdf:RDF` fixture whose items are siblings of `channel` (not nested inside it), produces one `RawDoc` per item — checked with a new RDF fixture literal, distinct from the existing `rssBody()`, shaped like Planalto's real feed (`<rdf:RDF>` root with an `xmlns:dc` declaration, a `<channel>` containing no items, and one or more `<item rdf:about="...">` elements as top-level siblings carrying `<title>`, `<link>`, `<description>`, `<content:encoded>` and `<dc:date>`).

A `toDoc` call on an RDF item whose `dc:date` is set (e.g. `2026-09-02T18:34:00Z`) and whose `pubDate` is absent produces a `publishedAt` matching that date, not the current time — asserted by comparing the parsed date (year/month/day, or an exact ISO match) against the fixture's `dc:date` value, not merely that `publishedAt` is a truthy string.

An RDF item with neither `pubDate` nor `dc:date` still produces a `RawDoc` (not `null`, no thrown error), `publishedAt` falling back to the current time — the same code path RSS 2.0 already exercises for a missing `pubDate`.

`src/collectors/oficial.ts`'s `feeds` array includes the Planalto URL (`https://www.gov.br/planalto/pt-br/acompanhe-o-planalto/noticias/RSS`) as its 5th entry, and the parametrized `oficial` case in `test/collectors-rss.test.ts` (the `cases` array's `feedCount`) is updated from `4` to `5`.

Every `oficial` doc, Planalto's included, still carries `source: 'oficial'` and no `tone` field — covered by the existing per-family assertion loop (`describe('rss/juridico/oficial/nicho — ...')`), which needs no new assertion beyond the count bump in AC4.

The docs state, in `docsText` terms (any page, not tied to a heading or file): Planalto's feed is part of the `oficial` family, and `oficial` (or `rss.ts`) reads at least one RDF (RSS 1.0) feed. `test/docs-drift.test.ts` already has a per-collector row check and a default-source-agreement check (`'every collector has a row in the source table'`, `'the source table agrees with defaultSources'`) — those are unaffected by this issue (the `oficial` row and its `defaultSources` membership do not change) and need no new criterion. This criterion is new because the fact that `oficial` now includes an RDF feed, and that Planalto specifically is no longer excluded, is not yet written down anywhere.

`docsText` no longer states that Planalto's feed is unsupported, excluded, or that `rss.ts`'s parser assumes RSS 2.0 for every feed — checked as the absence of that claim, not the absence of one particular sentence or file location. Note for the builder: `test/docs-drift.test.ts` already has a test titled `'press families (issue #22): ... and the RDF/Planalto exclusion'` that only asserts the words "RDF" and "Planalto" appear somewhere in `docsText` — it does not assert exclusion, so it keeps passing once the prose is rewritten to describe inclusion instead. The title is now stale prose describing a fact that no longer holds; rename it in the same PR (e.g. drop "exclusion" from the title) so a future reader isn't misled — this is a docs-hygiene fix bundled into this PR, not a separate acceptance criterion, since a test title never itself gates a test.
